metadata.title: How Google Docs Lets Two People Type in the Same Sentence
metadata.narration_policy: Narration is SCRIPT.md verbatim, one script section per beat. Beat IDs B01-B10 match script sections 1-10; BVDT, BHTF and BOUT are sections 11, 12 and 13. On-screen-only lines and source tags in SCRIPT.md are not narrated.
metadata.visual_policy: Simple illustrative graphics only: two plain browser windows, the letters a b c, operations moving to a server, a revision log, cursors, two copies that change on their own and end up the same. No Google logo, no Google Docs interface screenshots or colour scheme, no other branding. The windows are drawn rectangles with a text line, not a copy of any product's interface. Every example is an illustration, not data. The Claude composer, verdict page and channel mark are redrawn bookends, not screenshots.
metadata.on_screen_text_note: Control Z is spoken; the on-screen key chip and text show Ctrl+Z, as SCRIPT.md allows.
metadata.library_check: Searched with ./art scenes first, for: two browser windows sharing a document, operations sent to a server and acknowledged, revision log history list, typed-then-corrected overview, text cursors of two collaborators, two copies changing on their own and ending up the same, letters a b c insert and delete shift, two copies client and server sync, keyboard key press Ctrl Z undo, packets travelling between client and server, two versions merge in any order without a central server, slow connection delayed text arriving late, two edits side by side conflict merge. Reused: ClaudeComposerAsk, BrutalistHesitantWriter, ClaudeVerdictArtifact, LogoOutro (and their 916 variants). No library match for the a-b-c insert-and-delete example, the client/server change flow, the revision log, cursors with undo, two copies changing on their own and ending up the same, or the slow-connection and two-rewrites pictures, so B02 and B04-B10 are custom Manim scenes. Leads read (from their search descriptions) and rejected: BrowserCapture (a real captured web page, not allowed here), LectureDocumentTree (a source traversal tree), HaiBrutalistE10Revise (a video revision loop), SourcedExhibit (a fixed exhibit for another film), the McpServer and McpInt figures (MCP deployment diagrams).

portrait_layout.rule: In 9:16, all text and labels sit above 86% of the frame height (y < 0.86 * H), leaving the bottom 14% empty.

metadata.portrait_text_rule: Portrait scenes never scale text: font sizes are set directly, with a 32 pt floor (x-height about 87 px at 2160 px wide, above the 72 px rule), and every line sits above 86% of the frame height.
